#### 1. autosomal recessive cutis laxa type 2C  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.439)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9639288)

**Proposed mechanism:** FLCN (HGNC:27494) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal lung morphology (HP:0002105); FLCN (HGNC:27494) —LEADS_TO→ Spontaneous pneumothorax (HP:0002093); ATP6V1E1 (HGNC:703) —DISRUPTS→ Vacuolar ATPase function (GO:0016251); Vacuolar ATPase function (GO:0016251) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000288); Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000288) —DISRUPTS→ Cutis laxa (HP:0001063); Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000288) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal lung morphology (HP:0002105). Loss-of-function mutations in FLCN disrupt cellular processes leading to spontaneous pneumothorax and abnormal lung morphology. Separately, loss-of-function mutations in ATP6V1E1 disrupt the vacuolar ATPase complex and subsequent lysosomal acidification, resulting in cutis laxa and abnormal lung morphology. The convergence is on the shared pathway of maintaining lysosomal function and cellular integrity, which is critical for both lung and connective tissue health.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in FLCN with a minor allele frequency > 0.001 in gnomAD, or demonstration that ATP6V1E1 function is entirely independent of FLCN function in lung epithelial cells. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on vacuolar ATPase function and lysosomal homeostasis for lung and connective tissue integrity could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both spontaneous pneumothorax and cutis laxa, potentially involving modulators of lysosomal function or proton pump activity.

Loss-of-function mutations in FLCN (familial spontaneous pneumothorax) and RRAGC (Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome) disrupt the function of the Ragulator complex, leading to decreased mTORC1 signaling. This dysregulation impacts cellular processes, manifesting as spontaneous pneumothorax in the lungs and abnormal cellular growth and intellectual disability in Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in FLCN or RRAGC do not affect the Ragulator complex or mTORC1 signaling in cellular or animal models, or that the observed phenotypes in each disease arise from entirely independent pathways unrelated to mTORC1 dysregulation. _(variant: Identification of common loss-of-function variants in FLCN or RRAGC in the general population (gnomAD frequency > 1%) would challenge their role as rare disease-causing genes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link through the Ragulator complex and mTORC1 signaling pathway opens avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting mTORC1 activity to potentially ameliorate aspects of both familial spontaneous pneumothorax and Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** If studies demonstrate that FLCN and RRAGD act in completely independent cellular pathways that do not converge at any level of the autophagy machinery, or if mutations in FLCN do not affect autophagy flux while mutations in RRAGD do, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.1%) in FLCN or RRAGD associated with either disease would challenge the rare variant hypothesis.)_
